turnaround_reason: Fox Factory was hit by post-COVID bike channel destocking and soft powersports/consumer demand, dropping from ~$30 toward a $13 low. The bet is that destocking is bottoming, powersports is reaccelerating, and a $50M cost program restores earnings power.
bullish_points: Destocking bottoming: management says inventory rebalancing 'really taken shape'; powersports +22.5% within Powered Vehicles Group
Big adjusted EPS beats (Q2 adj 0.37 vs 0.18; Q1 0.18 vs 0.08) with 12.7% adjusted EBITDA margin
Self-help: >$25M of gross savings captured in H1 toward a $50M 2026 target; net debt down $9.1M since year-end
Recovering screen mode with momentum (+15.5% over 30d) and forward P/E ~11.5
Diversified premium brand portfolio (FOX, Marucci, Method) with OEM + aftermarket + DTC channels
bearish_points: Revenue still declining (-4.5% TTM); GAAP profit margin -20% reflects impairment and weak absorption
Leverage is elevated (debt ~$680M, D/E ~102) for a cyclical with lumpy OEM order timing
Specialty Sports (bike) sales still falling YoY on OEM timing and channel destocking
Consumer-cyclical discretionary demand (bikes, trucks, powersports) is rate- and sentiment-sensitive; recovery could stall
catalyst: Q3 2026 earnings confirming destocking is over, SSG returning to growth, and cost savings dropping to the bottom line
suggested_trade: Small spot starter (~$21) on the destocking-inflection thesis; add on a confirmed return to revenue growth
key_risk: Bike/powersports demand stays weak so the 'destocking over' call proves premature and revenue keeps declining against a levered balance sheet
would_skip_if: Q3 shows SSG still shrinking or guidance cut, signaling demand (not just inventory) is the problem
